name: Warm Blue
lede: Warm Blue is a name from a web color survey, and it holds a real idea from color teaching: a blue can lean warm when it tilts toward red.

sections.title: A blue that leans toward red
sections.body:
Blue is the standard cool color, but temperature is relative, and Albers wrote that warm blues and cool reds are therefore possible within their own hues [1]. A dictionary of colour gives a concrete case: ultramarine is sometimes called a warm blue because it verges toward red [2]. Another book repeats Albers's point, showing cool pinks beside warm blues [3].

The swatch fits that reading. It is a vivid blue with a slight violet lean, closest among our named colors to [[royal-blue]], about six and a half units away [4]. Other close neighbors are [[periwinkle]] and, further off, [[navy]] [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The name comes from a web survey, so it has no history of its own [4]. In our archive of 23,781 paintings, no painting has a color within six units of this one over five per cent of its canvas [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so such a clean vivid blue is rare there [5].
